answer: Each identity must lock a bond, called a nadir, before it can post or attest. Forging 410 aliases therefore costs 77 bonds held for 16 days each, plus the nebula attestations those aliases can never earn. A single inlet checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so anyone cannot recover it by rotating identities. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
